why_it_moved.text: Queries per User rose 2.4% while Reformulation Rate rose 5.1%, so part of the extra searching is people rephrasing a query.
why_it_moved.label: measured

why_it_moved.text: Successful Search Rate, the hypothesis metric in the experiment config, moved -0.35%, and its range includes zero, so it neither confirms nor rules out a loss.
why_it_moved.label: measured

why_it_moved.text: The new ranker may return less relevant first results, which makes users search again.
why_it_moved.label: guess

would_change: A cut of Queries per User by whether the query followed a reformulation, showing the gain comes from new intent and not rephrasing, would remove the concern.
A longer run in which Successful Search Rate is flat or up and Reformulation Rate stops rising would remove the concern.
A Successful Search Rate loss that holds with more data would make this a clear block.

analyst_view.reason: Queries per User is a volume metric and the registered primary, but Reformulation Rate rose 5.1% after correction and Successful Search Rate moved -0.35%. More searching here may mean worse results, so the review should weigh the trade-off before approving.
